generations.name: Second generation electric drive (ED2)
generations.notes: 451 chassis, 16.5 kWh Tesla-supplied lithium-ion pack, 3.3 kW AC, no DC fast charging; 30 kW motor in the EPA 2011 rating. US lease/field-test car (US trials from late 2010, registrations to Dec 2012); only EPA rates it (MY2011), no NRCan row. Confidence: medium (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_electric_drive

generations.name: Third generation electric drive (ED3)
generations.notes: Still the 451 chassis, new 17.6 kWh Deutsche ACCUmotive pack and 55 kW motor (EPA) / 35 kW rated (NRCan). North American cars charge on J1772 at about 3.3 kW AC (the 22 kW option was Europe-only, general knowledge, not confirmed on a fetched page); no DC fast charging. US release May 2013 (MY2013). Wikipedia calls it MY2012-2016 globally. Confidence: medium (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_electric_drive

generations.name: Fourth generation (ED4, EQ fortwo from 2019)
generations.notes: New 453 chassis, 17.6 kWh pack carried over, 60 kW motor, 7.2 kW on-board charger in North America, no DC fast charging. US sales from Aug 2017 (MY2017); renamed EQ fortwo (MY2019 in EPA and NRCan, NRCan make "smart EQ"). smart left North America after MY2019. NRCan has no MY2017 row. Confidence: high (researched 2026-11-19, owner review pending). Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_electric_drive
